statement: Here a substring word[i..j) with 0 <= i <= j <= len(word) is called beautiful iff it contains at least one occurrence of each of 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' and for every k with i <= k < j-1, word[k] <= word[k+1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the maximum of the set containing 0 and all integers j-i such that 0 <= i <= j <= len(word) and word[i..j) is beautiful; equivalently, r is the length of a longest beautiful substring of word, or 0 if word has no beautiful substring.
preconditions: 1 <= len(word) <= 500000; every byte of word is one of 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' (ASCII codes 97, 101, 105, 111, 117).
